issues.description: The problem UML and description specify getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning a custom StudentCount type. This return-type mismatch is structural: students following the specification or tests expecting an int will be unable to match the solution's signature or compile against it.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the return type across all artifacts. Either change the solution's getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return int (e.g., return numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents) to match the UML/specification and template expectations, or update the problem statement, template signatures, and tests to document and require the StudentCount type consistently.

issues.description: The solution introduces a StudentCount class and uses it as the return type of getTotalNumberOfStudents(), but the problem statement and template do not mention or provide such a type. Introducing this additional type without documenting it in the exercise creates confusion and a structural mismatch between artifacts.
issues.suggestedFix: Either remove the StudentCount class and return a primitive int from getTotalNumberOfStudents() (and adjust solution accordingly), or update the problem statement and template to introduce and require the StudentCount type (including its API) so all artifacts consistently use the same type.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int (a primitive int), but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return a StudentCount object and introduces a StudentCount class. This represents the same conceptual entity (the total number of students) with a different identifier/type across artifacts and can confuse students: they will implement the method to return an int per the UML/instructions, while the provided solution uses a StudentCount wrapper.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the representation consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (sum of inscribed and guest students) to match the UML and problem text, removing the StudentCount wrapper; or (B) update the problem statement and UML to document and teach the StudentCount wrapper type (including its getValue() method) so students are expected to return a StudentCount instance.
